sections.heading: 1. Separate public discovery from permissioned proof
paragraphs: Start with a source registry, not a scraper. Public manifests, tariff schedules and court dockets reveal possible opportunities; they do not establish ownership, eligibility or collectible value. This desk maps 12 operational plays: manifest prospecting, HTS substitution screening, direct-identification tracing, export reconciliation, drawback packet assembly, liquidation monitoring, Post-Summary Correction triage, protest routing, settlement eligibility screening, accounts-payable evidence packaging, distribution reconciliation and authorized GPO shared-savings recovery. These are working mappings, not twelve independently verified income streams. Record each source's owner, access agreement, permitted uses, retrieval time, source-effective date, document hash and responsible reviewer. A Panjiva consignee match creates a research task, while an authorized ACE entry line and commercial invoice support an actual customs analysis. A settlement announcement creates a monitoring task, while the operative court order and administrator instructions establish claim requirements. Keep public discovery records outside client evidence folders until identity and authorization are resolved. Retain original downloads alongside parsed records so later corrections remain explainable. The directory below specifies desk polling targets separately from source publication timing; a daily poll cannot make a delayed upstream feed current. Assign every unresolved source limitation to a named work queue rather than converting it into an optimistic recovery estimate.

Use an enrichment waterfall that becomes more expensive only when evidence improves. First, identify the legal entity through its own website, secretary-of-state records and, for reporting companies, SEC filings. Second, inspect ImportGenius or Panjiva shipment records under the purchased license; ocean-manifest visibility does not cover every transport mode, confidential shipment or importer relationship. Third, request a narrow client-authorized ACE extract, broker statement and sample export packet. Fourth, obtain complete transaction histories only after the broker confirms a plausible statutory route. Illustratively, screening 100 entities at four minutes each consumes 6.7 analyst hours; reviewing 20 authorized samples at 30 minutes adds ten hours. At a planning rate of $45 per hour, that waterfall costs about $750 before commercial data charges. Those are workload assumptions, not vendor prices or expected conversion rates. Reject a name-only join when two subsidiaries share a brand. Require legal name, address history and a client-confirmed account or importer identifier. For settlement work, extend the identity graph to predecessor entities and acquired purchasing accounts, but obtain evidence of claim ownership before consolidation. A failed identity match returns to manual review; it never becomes a fabricated tax identifier or an inferred claimant authorization.

Treat retrieval engineering as an evidence-control function. Prefer documented APIs and authorized exports over browser automation, and never circumvent authentication, access restrictions or a provider's download controls. Store a per-host request budget, honor Retry-After, use exponential backoff with jitter and cache unchanged resources using ETag or Last-Modified where supported. The SEC ceiling is ten requests per second across the requester; a two-request-per-second desk cap leaves headroom but does not replace current access guidance. For sources without published quotas, begin with single-request concurrency and a five-second interval, then obtain permission before increasing throughput. A successful HTTP response does not prove completeness: compare row counts, reporting periods and source totals before accepting a refresh. Record whether latency measures publication delay, retrieval delay or analyst review delay. When a feed fails, preserve the last verified snapshot, flag its age and route deadline-sensitive matters to the broker or administrator directly. Do not silently substitute a secondary database for an operative tariff schedule or court order. Keep encrypted client evidence separate from public caches, restrict access by matter, and remove credentials from logs. Every directory entry needs an owner who can explain both its commercial terms and its evidentiary limits.

sections.heading: 2. Build line-level joins that survive an adversarial document review
paragraphs: Build the pipeline around immutable source objects and reversible transformations. A modest desk can use encrypted object storage, SQLite for local investigation, PostgreSQL for shared case records and Git for parser changes; select deployment tools according to actual operating capacity. Python's csv, decimal, hashlib, datetime and sqlite3 modules cover a substantial first implementation without subscription sprawl. Create separate tables for entities, authorizations, entry lines, tariff versions, export events, invoice lines, settlement matters, claim packets and cash receipts. Each derived record must retain source-object hash, source row, transformation version and reviewer decision. Use Decimal for currency and explicit unit codes for quantities. Preserve the original date string alongside its parsed date, particularly when documents mix month-first and day-first conventions. A file checksum proves that bytes stayed unchanged, not that the underlying commercial event occurred. Reconcile line totals to broker statements or client ledgers before proceeding. Quarantine malformed rows instead of dropping them. Assign stable ingestion keys so the same invoice imported twice does not double a potential recovery. If the client replaces a file, store both versions and explain the delta rather than overwriting the earlier evidence. This architecture makes corrections inspectable without turning an analyst's spreadsheet into the sole system of record.

Separate candidate matching from legal eligibility. For manifest prospecting, normalize names and addresses but retain the original strings; a fuzzy match should generate a review queue, never a file-ready importer identity. For direct-identification tracing and export reconciliation, connect authorized entry lines to inventory movements, invoices and export transport evidence using the identification method applicable to the claim. For HTS substitution screening, an eight-digit concordance is only a candidate filter: subsection-specific rules, special classifications, quantity limitations and duty comparisons still require broker review. Illustratively, 2,400 entry lines reduced to 360 candidate lines by product and date filters create a manageable work queue. If 90 lack export support and 30 fail legal screening, 240 remain for documentation, not automatic payment. At eight minutes per retained line, review requires 32 hours; at $45 per hour, direct analyst labor is $1,440. Preserve rejected lines with reason codes so the next import does not resurrect them. Do not manufacture a missing export date from an invoice date. Request carrier records or client transport archives, and defer unsupported quantities. Drawback packet assembly succeeds when every claimed quantity has a reproducible allocation and no prior claim has already consumed the same entitlement.

Run diagnostic tests before analysts inspect individual opportunities. Check duplicate entry-line keys, negative quantities, currencies outside the contract, impossible date sequences, unmatched unit conversions and multiple allocations of the same exported quantity. Build an exception report for invoice totals that diverge from ledger controls by more than a documented rounding tolerance. For settlement eligibility and accounts-payable evidence packaging, test transaction dates against the court-defined class period, map product descriptions to included products and exclude credits or reversals according to administrator instructions. A $500,000 purchase ledger with $20,000 of excluded credits supports $480,000 of screened purchases, not a $480,000 expected distribution. Store the allocation formula separately because settlement payments may depend on approved claims, caps and deductions that remain unresolved. For liquidation monitoring, calculate deadlines from verified legal events, maintain jurisdiction-appropriate calendars and display source documents next to every computed date. A parser test suite should include amended entries, split shipments, duplicate filenames and acquired entities sharing an address. Use synthetic fixtures for development and restrict production evidence to authorized staff. When a test fails, freeze the affected output partition, preserve the diagnostic report and continue unrelated matters rather than silently passing contaminated records downstream.

sections.heading: 3. Give each recovery lane its own legal clock and cash model
paragraphs: The drawback lane starts with 19 U.S.C. § 1313 and the applicable provisions of 19 CFR Part 190, not a universal refund percentage applied to every import charge. Many eligible claims recover 99% of qualifying duties, taxes and fees, but the statutory route, exclusions and comparison rules control the actual base. Screen antidumping and countervailing duties out of drawback calculations, and examine each additional tariff regime independently; never classify every Chapter 99 charge as either eligible or barred. For an illustrative file with $100,000 of fully eligible duty and no limiting adjustment, a 99% recovery produces $99,000 for the client before the agreed fee. A 30% contingency produces $29,700 of operator revenue. Budgeting 40 documentation hours at $45 plus a hypothetical $2,000 broker charge leaves $25,900 before other costs; obtain actual quotes before accepting the engagement. Check the import-based five-year claim period and subsection-specific export or destruction conditions. Accelerated payment requires CBP approval and appropriate bond coverage; ordinary processing does not create an identical incremental bond requirement. Use a six-to-eighteen-month collection assumption for initial planning, explicitly replacing it with broker-supported case estimates. Missing export traces trigger partial exclusion or deferral, not invented shipment evidence.

The tariff-refund lane must distinguish Post-Summary Corrections from protests. PSC triage concerns eligible unliquidated entries and current ACE program rules; protest routing concerns protestable decisions under 19 U.S.C. § 1514 and applicable procedures in 19 CFR Part 174. The usual PSC window is within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever deadline arrives first, subject to current CBP rules and entry circumstances. A protest generally must be filed within 180 days after liquidation or the relevant protestable decision. Store those as distinct event-driven clocks rather than a single five-year recovery horizon. Illustratively, $80,000 of verified overpaid duties, fully refunded, produces a $24,000 fee at 30%. Twenty-four documentation hours at $45 and a hypothetical $1,500 specialist charge leave $21,420 before other costs. A PSC or protest does not itself require a drawback accelerated-payment bond, although the underlying import bond and disputed liabilities remain relevant. Plan three-to-twelve months for a straightforward refund while recognizing contested matters can take substantially longer. Route formal work through the licensed customs broker or trade counsel with valid authority. If liquidation timing defeats PSC eligibility, assess an available protest route immediately instead of backdating an amendment.

The settled antitrust lane begins with the operative class definition, allocation plan and administrator instructions, not an advertised gross settlement fund. Settlement eligibility screening identifies the claimant, covered purchases, class period and exclusions; accounts-payable evidence packaging establishes the supported transaction base. Distribution reconciliation then matches actual payments to approved claims. The collectible contingency base is the claimant's realized distribution under the engagement, not its total purchases or the court's aggregate fund. Illustratively, a $40,000 received distribution generates a $12,000 fee at 30%. Twelve documentation hours at $45 and a hypothetical $300 secure-delivery allocation leave $11,160 before other costs. There is ordinarily no customs surety bond for this lane. Planning may require six-to-twenty-four months after submission, with appeals, deficiencies or supplemental distributions extending the period. Capture court-required third-party filer disclosures and explain that eligible claimants may submit directly without paying a recovery-service fee. Do not claim administrator affiliation or submit duplicate claims to improve perceived odds. These three examples are independent unit models, not components of the canonical annual scorecard. Each requires its own evidence cost, collection forecast and fee-recognition event. When eligibility is disputed, seek administrator clarification, preserve the reply and suspend any related fee demand.

sections.heading: 4. Operate the tool stack against earned fees, not impressive transaction volume
paragraphs: The twelfth mapped play is private_b2b_gpo_umbrella_rebate_arbitrage, a TRACK_1 adjacent spend-recovery workflow rather than a customs remedy. Pool 10,000–75,000+ seats and indirect spend across hundreds of SMB members only through authorized master GPO brackets, using Una, OMNIA or an eligible private vertical SaaS, parcel or telecom program. Seat totals describe negotiating scale; they are not revenue. Quarter-end comparisons may use Vendr or Tropic methodologies and licensed benchmark access, but confidential customer benchmarks cannot be presumed transferable. Target ranges of 3%–12% vendor-paid administrative rebates and 25%–35% Year-1 shared-savings fees require contract-level verification. For one illustrative member cohort, a documented $120,000 baseline reduced to $108,000 yields $12,000 gross savings; a 30% shared-savings fee is $3,600, leaving $8,400 before other member costs. A separate 3% administrative rebate on $108,000 eligible paid spend is $3,240 only if the supplier agreement permits that base and compensation. Disclose both payments and any required offsets; never add a retained vendor rebate to client savings. Keep this adjacent example outside the canonical customs-and-settlement revenue cases. If eligibility or baseline calculations are disputed, suspend fees, reconcile with members and suppliers, refund unearned amounts and move affected members to eligible purchasing agreements.

Tie subscriptions and staffing to the canonical Formula v2.0 scorecard, not to gross merchandise value or an administrator's settlement pool. Conservative annual earned-fee revenue is $110,000; the 32% margin yields $35,200 owner profit and $74,800 total modeled costs. Base revenue is $515,000; the 45.0% margin yields $231,750 owner profit and $283,250 costs. Scaled revenue is $920,000; the 58% margin yields $533,600 owner profit and $386,400 costs. Conservative and Base each use one full-time operator plus three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time staff plus four contractors. Contractor count does not imply six full-time salaries. Treat the $1,500–$9,500 monthly operating-expense range as a planning category, not a substitute for all annual costs, including variable specialist work. The $8,000–$35,000 startup range funds setup and working capacity; a first engagement in one to three months does not mean a refund arrives then. Under the stated revenue basis, gross revenue means the operator's earned fees, not the client's recovered principal. If an arrangement requires principal-versus-agent assessment under ASC 606, apply the appropriate presentation to that arrangement rather than mechanically changing these supplied cases. Maintain separate cash, earned-fee and client-recovery ledgers so timing differences cannot inflate apparent profitability.

Use a weekly operating review to decide which tools deserve renewal. Measure verified opportunities per paid source, analyst minutes per supported line, unresolved evidence age, deadline exceptions, accepted packets, realized distributions and collected fees. A $600 monthly data allocation costs $7,200 annually; at a 30% fee, it requires $24,000 of incremental realized client recoveries merely to cover that subscription before labor. That is a diagnostic hurdle, not a forecast or a vendor price quote. Compare the paid source against a public-data and client-export control sample before attributing wins. Use OpenRefine for reversible entity cleanup, SQLite queries for duplicate detection and a broker-reviewed checklist for tariff logic; no dashboard replaces the specialist's eligibility decision. Track workload separately from money: 30 signed engagements with incomplete export records can consume more capacity than ten fully documented claims. Close abandoned matters with a reason code and retention schedule, then remove unnecessary access. Test restoration of encrypted backups quarterly and verify that departed contractors lose matter permissions promptly. The durable information edge is not a secret database. It is the ability to turn authorized, time-stamped records into a reproducible packet, collect the resulting earned fee and explain every rejected dollar.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #44, Customs Duty Drawback, Tariff Refund & Antitrust Claim Recovery, holds Rank #03 of 49 with a 95/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 12 mapped plays. This chapter turns that opportunity into three separately controlled recovery lanes: Part 190 drawback, liquidation-sensitive tariff corrections and protests, and court-administered B2B settlement claims. Build contracts around collected proceeds, licensed representation, claimant-controlled payments, documented eligibility, and state-specific outreach rules. Annual owner net profit is $35,200 Conservative, $231,750 Base, and $533,600 Scaled; these figures arise from earned contingency fees, never recovered duty principal or settlement pools. The public_record_api_intelligence play supplies evidence-backed prospect signals, while professional filing authority, source provenance, and direct-filing disclosures keep acquisition from becoming unauthorized representation.

sections.heading: 1. Separate eligibility, authority, and cash mechanics before quoting a fee
paragraphs: Treat drawback as a statutory matching business, not a generic tariff rebate. Under 19 U.S.C. § 1313 and 19 CFR Part 190, identify the applicable manufacturing, unused-merchandise, rejected-merchandise, or other authorized provision before building the population. Unused-merchandise substitution under § 1313(j)(2) requires more than a convenient eight-digit HTS match; apply the statutory description restrictions, possession requirements, export or destruction conditions, and valuation limits. An ImportGenius or Panjiva manifest establishes a lead, not paid duty, qualifying use, or export entitlement. Obtain ACE entry summaries, Form 7501 line detail, payment evidence, commercial invoices, export bills of lading, and the relevant transfer certificates. Exclude antidumping and countervailing duties and any other barred duty category; assess Section 301 and Section 232 treatment separately rather than applying one tariff rule. Illustratively, $400,000 of fully eligible duties at a 99% refund rate produces $396,000 of claimant recovery and a 30% fee of $118,800. A $12,000 documentation and broker budget leaves $106,800 before acquisition, overhead, and other case costs. Track the five-year statutory claim-completion limit against each import. Budget six to eighteen months for ordinary payment as a planning assumption, not an agency service commitment; accelerated payment requires separate privilege approval, adequate bond coverage, and recapture reserves.

Keep tariff correction and protest work in a separate deadline register. A Post-Summary Correction is an ACE correction mechanism for eligible unliquidated entries, not a protest and not a way to revive expired rights. Confirm current CBP eligibility and timing instructions; the ordinary PSC window is within 300 days of entry or fifteen days before scheduled liquidation, whichever comes first, subject to applicable exceptions. Once a protestable decision occurs, 19 U.S.C. § 1514 generally requires a protest within 180 days of liquidation or the relevant decision. Classification, valuation, origin, exclusion coverage, and preference claims require different evidence; some post-importation claims instead follow § 1520(d) and its own time limit. Route formal customs submissions through a Part 111 licensed customs broker or trade counsel with authority for the specific act and a valid Customs Power of Attorney where required. Do not assume an attorney may perform every category of customs business without a broker license. Illustratively, a documented $100,000 refund yields a $30,000 fee at 30%; a $4,500 evidence and professional-services budget leaves $25,500 before shared expenses. Model three to twelve months to receipt, then stress longer disputes. No separate drawback accelerated-payment bond attaches merely because this lane seeks a tariff refund.

For settled B2B antitrust claims, eligibility comes from the settlement agreement, class definition, court orders, claim form, and distribution protocol, not from the size of the announced fund. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23 governs class settlement procedure; the Clayton Act, including 15 U.S.C. § 15, supplies a substantive antitrust damages framework but does not make every business an eligible claimant. Match purchasing entities, covered products, transaction dates, exclusions, releases, and any assignment restrictions. Reconcile AP ledgers, processor statements, acquisitions, and duplicate submissions before the authorized claimant signs. Use the court-approved administrator's current instructions, disclose third-party assistance when required, and state plainly that the claimant may file directly at zero cost. A $60,000 actual distribution creates an $18,000 fee at 30%; a $2,400 ledger-packaging budget leaves $15,600 before shared expenses. Purchase volume is evidence, never operator revenue. Budget six to twenty-four months after a timely claim for planning, with longer delays possible during appeals or allocation disputes. Ordinary claim submission has no customs surety requirement. Counsel must handle legal objections, disputed ownership, or release interpretation. A closed deadline means checking an express late-claim process, not promising that an administrator will reopen the class.

callout.title: Protect evidence quality before purchasing filing capacity
callout.body: Most expensive failures begin with an apparently attractive recovery base that cannot survive a line-level entitlement test.
items: Ask the broker to review a ten-entry sample before pricing the entire drawback population; retain rejected examples as matcher test cases.
Store both scheduled and actual liquidation events; changing a scheduled date must not silently overwrite the protest deadline history.
Separate ordinary drawback receipts from accelerated payments so a bond-backed payment never appears operationally final merely because cash arrived.
Match settlement claims by legal entity, predecessor, and purchasing account before submission; preserve the administrator's duplicate-resolution correspondence.

sections.heading: 2. Contract for collected fees without purchasing authority you do not possess
paragraphs: Use a master services agreement with separate lane schedules, not one broad promise to recover everything. The scope clause should authorize administrative data collection, reconciliation, project coordination, and expressly identified claim preparation support. Reserve customs business to properly authorized professionals and legal representation to counsel; a private contract cannot create a license. Identify the claimant, importer of record, exporter, purchasing entity, and any predecessor separately. Have the broker obtain the Customs Power of Attorney directly from the appropriate principal under 19 CFR § 111.36 rather than treating the recovery operator as a substitute principal. The client should separately retain counsel when legal work is needed. State whether professional invoices are absorbed into the operator's contingency or require specifically authorized reimbursement; zero-upfront marketing cannot conceal a mandatory intake charge. Define a 25%–35% fee range with a signed case-specific percentage and an objectively identified recovery schedule. Sample wording: 'The service fee equals 30% of covered recovery cash actually received by Client, excluding unrelated refunds, unpaid awards, and amounts returned to the payor.' Specify treatment of interest, offsets, installments, withholding, and later reversals rather than leaving those issues to invoice-time negotiation. Preserve claimant ownership of the underlying recovery.

Build payment verification around claimant-controlled receipts. Prefer direct CBP or administrator payment to the claimant, followed by an invoice supported by remittance advice and a redacted bank credit. Do not change administrator bank instructions merely to simplify fee collection. If a professional holds funds, their applicable trust-account and professional rules control. Accelerated drawback payments require special drafting because cash receipt can precede final allowance: define a reserve, fee adjustment, and repayment mechanism for recapture rather than calling the initial payment permanently earned. An anti-circumvention clause should cover only scheduled opportunities materially developed during the engagement and a reasonable, stated tail period, such as twelve months subject to state-law review. Exclude independently documented preexisting claims and prohibit double billing with an incumbent provider. Termination must preserve the claimant's ability to meet deadlines, obtain their records, and change representatives. Allocate intellectual property precisely: the client owns source records and claim-specific deliverables; the operator retains preexisting matching code and generalized methods, with a usable license for any embedded material needed to maintain the claim. Prohibit resale of identifiable ledgers and prohibit model training on client records unless separately and expressly authorized. Document the subcontractor access list and deletion obligations.

Make liability and dispute terms operationally usable. A fee-based liability cap needs a negotiated floor and jurisdiction-specific enforceability review; carve out intentional misconduct and address confidentiality breaches, mishandled funds, and unauthorized filings explicitly. Do not let a narrow cap excuse a promised deadline-control service without explaining the allocation. Use a short notice and executive-resolution period, then a defined court venue or a clearly drafted arbitration process with costs, emergency relief, and evidence preservation addressed. Require clients to certify record accuracy without shifting responsibility for the operator's own transformations back onto them. The commercial schedule must reconcile to Formula v2.0: Conservative revenue of $110,000 less $74,800 total operating costs produces $35,200 at 32%; Base revenue of $515,000 less $283,250 produces $231,750 at 45.0%; Scaled revenue of $920,000 less $386,400 produces $533,600 at 58%. Staffing remains 1 FT + 3 C, 1 FT + 3 C, and 2 FT + 4 C respectively. These are annual earned-fee scenarios, not sums of the illustrative lane cases. Evaluate principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606 for pass-through professional services; do not book claimant recoveries or gross settlement pools as operator revenue, and do not apply a second retained-share haircut to the supplied fee totals.

sections.heading: 3. Build a jurisdiction matrix and an evidence-preserving intelligence queue
paragraphs: Federal customs authority does not erase state boundaries around legal services, collections, privacy, or finder contracts. California Business and Professions Code § 6125 and New York Judiciary Law § 478 illustrate restrictions on unlicensed legal practice; local rules also govern lawyer referral arrangements and fee sharing. The operator should earn a separate administrative-services fee, not a share of counsel's legal fee. If a public-record lead becomes a state unclaimed-property recovery, stop applying the customs contingency template. California Code of Civil Procedure § 1582 imposes restrictions on investigator agreements, including a 10% compensation ceiling and timing conditions; New York Abandoned Property Law § 1416 has its own agreement requirements and 15% ceiling. These are adjacent-lane rules, not caps on every customs or antitrust engagement. A probate docket may identify an estate-owned business claim, but it does not authorize the operator to represent the estate or decide succession. Confirm fiduciary authority through appropriate counsel. Assess collection-agency licensing if the actual service expands into collecting debts for others, rather than presuming every refund service falls within or outside those statutes. Record the claimant state, operating state, service location, property situs where relevant, and professional reviewer before selecting contractual terms.

Implement public_record_api_intelligence as a bounded prospecting and evidence pipeline. Ingest official court notices, public dockets, county business-related filings, probate registries, unclaimed-property ledgers, and permitted public APIs only for a defined lead hypothesis. A docket can reveal purchasing relationships or an authorized successor; an unclaimed-property listing can suggest a separate research task. Neither proves customs eligibility. Join those signals to permissioned ImportGenius or Panjiva records and client-supplied ACE exports only after obtaining appropriate access. Store source URL, retrieval time, license terms, entity-resolution confidence, and the human review decision. Illustrative weekly math is 500 records at $0.04 acquisition cost, or $20, plus three analyst hours at $35, or $105. If twenty qualified contacts produce four discovery calls, direct research cost is $31.25 per call before outreach software and selling time. At one signed engagement from those calls, research-only acquisition cost is $125; no recovery or revenue exists yet. If an API closes or access terms change, switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues. Under 5 U.S.C. § 552, request existing agency records; disclosure exemptions and processing delays mean FOIA is neither unrestricted access nor an instant substitute for client records.

Apply sector-specific evidence and communication rules before expanding outreach volume. Manufacturing drawback needs production traceability; resellers need possession and export evidence; related-party imports can require specialized valuation analysis. Interchange settlements require the particular administrator's merchant and processor definitions, not a generic claim that every card acceptor qualifies. For commercial email, 15 U.S.C. § 7704 requires accurate routing information, nondeceptive subjects, required advertisement identification unless an exception applies, a valid physical postal address, and a workable opt-out honored within ten business days. B2B targeting does not remove these duties. Calling and texting require channel-specific review under 47 U.S.C. § 227, 47 CFR § 64.1200, applicable state telephone-solicitation rules, and recording laws; do not infer permission from a published number. Default to manually reviewed business email rather than automated calls or texts. If California privacy-law thresholds and scope apply, assess Civil Code § 1798.100 requirements and applicable service-provider contract terms before sharing personal information. Retain drawback records under the applicable Part 190 period, generally three years after liquidation of the drawback claim under § 190.15, while separately honoring longer Part 163, court, contract, or preservation duties. A five-year claim window is not a universal record-deletion schedule.

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks before any client submission
callout.body: A complete sales file is insufficient. Release a claim packet only when authority, entitlement, timing, and payment controls are independently evidenced.
items: Verify the claimant's legal identity and signatory authority; confirm broker license, applicable permit, representation scope, and required Customs Power of Attorney.
Recompute eligibility from source records, remove barred duties or excluded purchases, and reconcile duplicate or previously claimed transactions.
Have a second reviewer confirm the lane-specific deadline, current filing instructions, retained evidence, and any accelerated-payment bond capacity.

sections.heading: 4. Use exact outreach language and a documented four-step intake
paragraphs: Use the following email body verbatim only after the sender's system appends the real business identity, valid physical postal address, and working unsubscribe mechanism. Subject: 'Commercial inquiry about your import refund records.' Body: 'This is a commercial solicitation for recovery-support services. We help businesses organize records for potential customs duty drawback and tariff refunds. Public shipment information may indicate relevant activity, but it does not establish your eligibility or any refund amount. Would your import manager consider a short records-screening call? Formal customs submissions are handled by an appropriately authorized licensed customs broker or trade counsel. Our engagement has no upfront service fee; any contingency percentage and permitted expenses are agreed in writing before work begins. We do not need passwords or unrestricted ACE access for an initial conversation. If this is irrelevant, reply stop or use the unsubscribe link and we will suppress further marketing.' Do not insert a projected refund from manifest value, and do not imply CBP affiliation. Route replies to a human who can distinguish an exporter, importer, broker, and domestic buyer. Preserve the exact sent version, source signal, delivery timestamp, and suppression event so a contractor cannot restart outreach after a prospect has opted out.

For a settled antitrust opportunity, use this discovery opening: 'We are an independent paid recovery-support provider, not the court, settlement administrator, or class counsel. The settlement's official materials determine eligibility, deadlines, releases, and distributions. You may file directly with the official administrator at zero cost. If you choose our help, our fee and scope will be stated in a separate agreement. May we first confirm your purchasing entity, covered transaction dates, and whether anyone has already filed for those purchases?' Send the verified official administrator link with the written follow-up and reproduce any court-required third-party filer disclosure exactly; the general script does not replace prescribed language. Then ask: 'Can your team export the relevant AP or processor records through your own authorized account? Please exclude unrelated employee and customer details. Who can certify the submission, and are there predecessor entities, assignments, releases, or overlapping providers we should flag?' Never call an estimate an allocated award. If asked whether hiring the operator is necessary, answer: 'No. Direct filing is available at zero cost; our paid service is optional administrative support.' If the administrator bars the proposed third-party arrangement, stop that arrangement instead of changing the claimant identity or hiding the provider.

Use discovery to kill weak cases early while preserving strong ones. Ask: 'Which entity paid the duty or made the covered purchases? What evidence links each entry or transaction to that entity? What is the earliest possible filing deadline? Has another provider, broker, or affiliate already claimed this recovery? Are any receipts provisional or subject to repayment?' Record answers as unverified statements until source documents support them. Do not promise that a broker can repair missing export evidence or that a court will accept reconstructed purchases. The four-step procedure below turns those questions into an auditable intake. Use encrypted client uploads, least-privilege workspaces, deterministic reconciliation scripts, and a separate exception register rather than collecting credentials by email. Every handoff should carry the claim identifier, responsible professional, evidence index, deadline basis, and unresolved exceptions. If the project fails eligibility screening, explain the specific missing condition and return usable records; do not replace the original lane with a different service without agreement. At receipt, compare approved claim, remittance, deposit, fee calculation, and any reserve before closing the file. Review monthly conversion by qualified lead, signed engagement, submitted claim, realized recovery, and collected fee so apparent pipeline growth cannot conceal stalled cash conversion.

sop_steps.title: Classify the lane and identify the rights holder
sop_steps.action: Open a separate claim record for drawback, tariff refund, or settlement recovery.
sop_steps.detail: Record legal entities, authorized signatory, controlling source, earliest deadline, incumbent providers, and the specific basis for entitlement. Quarantine adjacent unclaimed-property or estate matters for separate review.

sop_steps.title: Secure the engagement and professional authority
sop_steps.action: Sign the lane schedule and verify the required professional engagement.
sop_steps.detail: Confirm fee percentage, covered receipts, reversals, data rights, termination handoff, and required disclosures. The broker obtains the proper direct power of attorney; counsel confirms authority for legal work.

sop_steps.title: Reconcile evidence and independently verify submission readiness
sop_steps.action: Build the indexed packet and resolve exceptions before professional submission.
sop_steps.detail: Recompute line eligibility, document exclusions, check duplicates, validate deadline calculations, and confirm any bond-dependent payment assumptions. Retain professional review and the actual filing acknowledgment.

sop_steps.title: Verify cash, invoice the earned fee, and preserve the file
sop_steps.action: Match the claimant's receipt to the covered claim before calculating compensation.
sop_steps.detail: Reconcile remittance and deposit evidence, apply reserves and reversal terms, invoice only the agreed fee base, and retain records under the applicable lane-specific schedule and any preservation hold.

chapters.pull_quote: A recoverable dollar needs an entitled claimant, a preserved deadline, an authorized filer, and a contract that follows the cash.
action_checklist: Create three separate lane schedules with eligibility tests, receipt-based fees, documentation budgets, payment assumptions, and bond treatment.
Verify the customs broker's license and applicable permit, counsel's authorized scope, direct principal power of attorney, and professional handoff procedure.
Build entry-level and claim-level deadline registers with controlling event dates, independent verification, filing acknowledgments, and exception escalation.
Review state-specific legal-practice, finder-fee, privacy, and solicitation rules before expanding a recovery service or communication channel.
Deploy the outreach scripts with real sender details, suppression controls, verified administrator links, and required direct-at-zero-cost filing disclosures.
Reconcile earned fees and total costs to $35,200, $231,750, and $533,600 annual owner profit without recognizing claimant principal as revenue.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #44, Customs Duty Drawback, Tariff Refund & Antitrust Claim Recovery, ranks #03 of 49 with a 95/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps 12 operator plays into an evidence-first automation system: SEC triggers source prospects, manifest and export matching qualify recoveries, and controlled claim packaging compounds broker and accountant referrals. Keep drawback, tariff corrections or protests, and settled antitrust distributions in separate eligibility and cash ledgers. The canonical annual owner profit cases are $35,200 Conservative, $231,750 Base, and $533,600 Scaled. Automating more than 70% of repetitive minutes is a measured operating target, not permission for autonomous filing. Human specialists retain classification, deadline, claimant-authority, submission, and cash-release decisions; deterministic checks and replayable evidence keep scale defensible.

sections.heading: 1. Separate the three recovery lanes before automating evidence
paragraphs: Build a case ledger before buying another prospecting subscription. One full-time operator owns client intake, commercial decisions, and cash reconciliation; three contractors cover licensed customs brokerage, trade-counsel exceptions, and evidence engineering. These are capacity assignments, not interchangeable professional permissions. Give every matter a client identifier, lane identifier, authority record, source-document inventory, deadline record, and immutable event history. Python can normalize authorized ACE exports and CBP Form 7501 records into SQLite for a single-worker pilot; a managed relational database becomes appropriate when concurrent reviewers require transaction isolation and durable access controls. Store original documents separately with SHA-256 digests, versioned extraction output, and page coordinates. ImportGenius and Panjiva support discovery and shipment cross-checking, but a manifest is neither proof of paid duty nor authority to file. Request client-authorized entry summaries, payment evidence, commercial invoices, inventory records, and export evidence before promoting a lead into an eligible case. Restrict the LLM to extraction, document grouping, and draft explanations grounded in those records. Treat instructions found inside PDFs, spreadsheets, and email attachments as document content, never executable instructions. Keep credentials outside prompts and give each contractor only the assigned client workspace. The operator should always be able to reproduce a match without the model.

The drawback lane begins with 19 U.S.C. § 1313 and the applicable subsection, not an eight-digit tariff-code coincidence. For unused-merchandise substitution under subsection (j)(2), evaluate the statutory classification conditions, applicable descriptive limitations, possession and use facts, export or destruction evidence, and the lesser-of calculation where required. Matching HTS codes merely proposes candidates. Exclude antidumping and countervailing duties from drawback; inspect the governing authority for each additional tariff component instead of assuming every surcharge qualifies. Section 232 restrictions require separate treatment from otherwise eligible Section 301 duties. Calendar the five-year claim-completion limit under subsection (r) alongside the relevant export and evidence requirements. A $100,000 eligible duty amount can support up to $99,000 of drawback where the 99% rule applies; at a 30% contingency, that produces $29,700 of operator fees, not $100,000 of revenue. Budget an illustrative $1,200 for document reconstruction and broker preparation against that matter. Accelerated payment introduces approval, bond sufficiency, and repayment exposure under 19 CFR Part 190; ordinary processing should remain available when acceleration is unavailable. Do not invent one universal bond amount. Obtain the broker's case-specific requirement and surety pricing before forecasting cash, and retain records for the applicable regulatory period.

The tariff-refund lane separates an ACE Post-Summary Correction from a protest under 19 U.S.C. § 1514. A PSC generally addresses an eligible unliquidated entry within ACE timing rules, commonly 300 days after entry or 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever comes first; confirm the operative program rules and entry-specific status. A protest generally has a 180-day statutory window after liquidation or another protestable decision. Neither workflow inherits drawback's five-year calendar. An illustrative $40,000 realized refund yields $12,000 at 30%, with $900 of document and specialist preparation reserved separately. Existing entry-bond obligations remain relevant, but do not price a new drawback accelerated-payment bond into every protest. The settlement lane instead follows the court-approved class definition, purchase period, release, allocation method, and administrator instructions. AP invoices or merchant-processing statements establish eligible activity; they do not establish the eventual distribution. An illustrative $20,000 actual distribution yields $6,000 at 30%, with $300 of preparation cost and no customs surety bond. Use planning ranges of 6–18 months for ordinary drawback, 3–12 months for tariff refunds, and 12–36 months for settlement distributions. These are sensitivity assumptions, not agency schedules; accelerated payment and litigation can materially change timing. Disclose direct, zero-cost claimant filing and any court-required third-party filer information.

callout.title: Four checks before any consequential submission
callout.body: Automation may prepare a packet; the authorized specialist must resolve these checks before transmission.
items: Confirm the importer or claimant owns the recovery right, the engagement identifies the fee base, and the broker holds a valid Customs Power of Attorney where required.

sections.heading: 2. Implement seven acquisition and evidence plays with deterministic checks
paragraphs: Map the supplied sec_edgar_8k_vendor_trigger_arbitrage play to an acquisition queue, not an eligibility engine. Consume SEC EDGAR latest-filings feeds and supported JSON endpoints; use Form D notices to identify private Regulation D raises and Form 8-K Items 5.02, 1.01, and 2.01 to flag leadership changes, material agreements, and completed acquisitions. Company submissions JSON is useful for monitored issuers but is not a universal real-time feed. Normalize accession numbers, issuer CIKs, filing timestamps, items, and source links. A Python worker can score whether an issuer has a plausible importer, exporter, or eligible purchasing footprint, then draft a source-linked message for human review. A raise or acquisition proves no recoverable duty or class membership. Target sub-hour preparation during staffed hours; do not promise outreach before every commercial database. For an illustrative daily batch, 100 filings at $0.02 extraction cost plus ten three-minute reviews at $60 hourly cost equals $32, or $3.20 per reviewed prospect. Enforce an aggregate token bucket of five requests per second, identify the requester, honor SEC access guidance, and back off on throttling. Mirror available SEC bulk ZIP releases and index archives nightly for historical lookbacks; those archives do not replace the live-feed freshness check.

The next six plays turn discovery into defensible packets: manifest_entry_match, export_bol_trace, hts8_substitution_reconcile, psc_protest_router, ap_settlement_packager, and duplicate_recovery_guard. These are chapter-local implementation identifiers, not additional supplied catalog identifiers. Match authorized ImportGenius or Panjiva exports to ACE entry lines using importer identity, shipment dates, bill references, quantities, and product attributes. Licensing and available export interfaces determine ingestion; do not assume either vendor grants unrestricted API access. Normalize HTS values as text so leading zeros survive. Use decimal.Decimal for duty and fee arithmetic, preserving currency and unit conversions in separate fields. The export reconciler joins bills of lading, invoices, departure evidence, and inventory movement; it should expose missing links rather than manufacture a continuous trace. The substitution worker proposes eight-digit matches and calculates quantity allocations, while the broker evaluates legal eligibility and claim methodology. For settlements, QuickBooks or NetSuite exports identify purchases; interchange matters may require acquirer statements and merchant identifiers instead. Record excluded credits, refunds, unrelated entities, and purchases outside the class period. Allocate each entry quantity or purchase row to a recovery ledger with explicit status. A second proposed claim against the same source becomes an exception, not another forecast win. Retain unmatched records for targeted client questions.

Implement webhooks as authenticated intake events with a replay-safe queue. Verify the provider's documented signature over the raw request body, check timestamps where supported, and reject oversized or unexpected payload types. Calculate an idempotency key from client identifier, source identifier, source digest, and workflow version; enforce uniqueness inside the same database transaction that creates the job. A changed document must generate a new version without erasing its predecessor. Acknowledge receipt only after durable enqueueing, then let a worker extract, normalize, validate, and route the result. Python's hashlib, hmac, json, sqlite3, decimal, and urllib modules support a modest prototype without a sprawling dependency chain. For an illustrative 100-document batch, budget $0.80 for OCR, $0.20 for bounded LLM extraction, $0.50 for compute and storage, $2.00 for allocated data access, and $3.00 for average retry overhead: $6.50 machine cost. Ten minutes of human QA at $60 hourly adds $10, giving $16.50 before substantive case preparation. These are adjustable planning inputs rather than vendor quotes. Maintain source spans for extracted amounts, reject malformed structured output, and route low-confidence documents to manual entry. Never retry an external filing merely because the network timed out; reconcile its receipt first.

sop_steps.title: Authenticate and preserve the source
sop_steps.action: Validate the intake event and durably store its original evidence.
sop_steps.detail: Apply client access boundaries, retain the raw payload digest, and create a versioned source record before acknowledging delivery.

sop_steps.title: Extract and reconcile deterministically
sop_steps.action: Generate structured fields, then reconcile identities, quantities, dates, and money.
sop_steps.detail: Use source spans, Decimal arithmetic, explicit unit conversions, and allocation uniqueness checks; treat model output as proposed data.

sop_steps.title: Resolve professional judgment exceptions
sop_steps.action: Route eligibility, deadline, authority, and disclosure decisions to the responsible specialist.
sop_steps.detail: Record the reviewer, reviewed source versions, decision basis, and release time; changed evidence invalidates the previous release.

sop_steps.title: Submit once and reconcile receipts
sop_steps.action: Have the authorized filer transmit the packet and attach the external receipt.

sections.heading: 3. Add five distribution and control plays without automating judgment
paragraphs: Complete the twelve-play map with deadline_receipt_monitor, evidence_packet_builder, broker_accountant_referral_loop, programmatic_eligibility_content, and cash_fee_reconciler. These five chapter-local identifiers connect operational quality to repeatable distribution. The deadline monitor stores both the legally significant event and its documented source, then computes internal checkpoints at 60, 30, 14, and seven days before the controlling date when that lead time exists. The broker or counsel confirms the actual deadline; a scheduler cannot resolve an ambiguous liquidation event. The packet builder produces a manifest of evidence, calculations, missing-document exceptions, and signed authority without silently submitting anything. The referral loop sends authorized status summaries to introducing brokers or accountants, showing documents obtained, qualified matters, and realized outcomes without exposing another client's records. Programmatic content publishes carefully reviewed explanations of recurring documentation problems, each linking to a narrow intake worksheet. The cash reconciler matches actual agency or administrator payments to fee terms and invoices. Each play must have one accountable owner and a measurable completion event. Separate drafted, reviewed, submitted, accepted, paid, and invoiced states; treating an uploaded packet as collected revenue is the quickest way to manufacture a misleading dashboard. Preserve revisions when an administrator changes forms or a broker changes the claim calculation.

Measure the automation target in repetitive labor minutes rather than document counts. Time a representative weekly cohort before deployment: assume 1,000 minutes spent on research, normalization, matching, follow-up drafting, packet assembly, and routine status checks. After deployment, suppose those same tasks require 250 human minutes, including exception handling. The reduction is 750 divided by 1,000, or 75%; retain a separate 120-minute consequential-review budget that the automation target does not erase. Total human time then falls from 1,120 to 370 minutes, a smaller 67.0% reduction across all work. This distinction prevents a headline efficiency claim from hiding broker review. Segment measurements by lane, document quality, and matter complexity; a clean recurring importer should not conceal a difficult inherited settlement ledger. Require complete packet review during the pilot, then reduce only low-risk extraction sampling after measured error rates support it. Always review eligibility, deadline calculations, claimant authority, payment instructions, and external submission. Track material error rate, rejected packets, review minutes, and collected fees per reviewed case together. A model that saves two minutes but creates one additional $300 reconstruction task every ten cases destroys $28 of value per case at a $60 hourly labor rate. Rework belongs in the efficiency denominator.

Design failure recovery before allowing unattended overnight processing. Keep source ingestion, extraction, reconciliation, review, and transmission in separate states with explicit retry policies. Retry transient vendor failures with bounded exponential backoff and jitter; move repeated failures into a visible dead-letter queue rather than dropping them. If a data subscription expires, continue processing already licensed client records and suspend enrichment instead of scraping around access restrictions. If the LLM endpoint fails, use deterministic CSV ingestion and manual document entry for deadline-sensitive matters. If OCR quality deteriorates, request original electronic records rather than repeatedly paying to interpret an unreadable scan. Store money fields as strings until validated Decimal conversion, and reject unsupported currency assumptions. A daily exception digest should identify the responsible person, earliest controlling date, missing evidence, and next action. Reserve capacity for urgent manual cases rather than scheduling the team at full theoretical utilization. Test restore procedures using a permitted sample workspace, including document hashes and allocation history; a database backup without its evidence objects cannot reconstruct the claim. For example, one two-hour outage at $60 hourly costs $120 in direct recovery labor. Compare that with the exposure from a missed filing window, not merely the monthly hosting charge.

callout.title: Veteran tactics that protect small-team throughput
callout.body: The best automation advantage is reducing evidence friction before the specialist opens the matter.
items: Ask recurring importers for stable SKU-to-HTS mappings and original entry-line exports; preserve historical mapping versions because current classifications cannot silently rewrite earlier entries.
Maintain separate clocks for importation, export, liquidation, protestable decisions, and settlement deadlines; never label a single spreadsheet column simply deadline.
Ask the broker to preflight accelerated-payment privileges and bond headroom before selling faster cash conversion; model ordinary processing when capacity is constrained.

For interchange claims, reconcile merchant identifiers across acquirers and ownership changes before summing statements; duplicate identifiers and predecessor entities regularly distort purchase bases.

sections.heading: 4. Compound qualified distribution while reconciling every dollar
paragraphs: Use three distribution loops with distinct attribution: timely outbound, programmatic education, and trusted introductions. SEC-triggered outbound should reference the actual filing event and offer a bounded evidence assessment, not assert that the issuer is owed money. Follow 15 U.S.C. § 7704 for commercial email, including accurate routing information, a valid postal address, a working opt-out mechanism, and timely suppression. Maintain suppression centrally across contractors and sending accounts. The content loop turns repeated client questions into source-linked pages about export trace gaps, PSC timing, or settlement documentation, with human review before publication. Avoid bulk-generated pages that invent eligibility or reproduce confidential purchase records. The referral loop begins after an actual operational win: a clean packet, a resolved evidence defect, or a collected recovery. Obtain permission before sharing even an anonymized case example when commercial facts could identify the client. As an illustrative monthly funnel, ten partners each produce two introductions; 20 introductions at 40% qualified become eight opportunities, and eight at 25% signed become two engagements. At $12,000 expected earned fees each, the cohort contains $24,000 of potential fees before recovery risk and delay. Do not annualize this pipeline into recognized revenue. Track signed, collectible, and collected cohorts separately.

Reconcile the scorecard using earned contingency fees, never importer duty principal or gross settlement pools. Conservative revenue is $110,000 with $74,800 of annual costs, leaving $35,200 at 32% for 1 FT + 3 C. Base revenue is $515,000 with $283,250 of costs, leaving $231,750 at 45.0% for the same four-person structure. Scaled revenue is $920,000 with $386,400 of costs, leaving $533,600 at 58% for 2 FT + 4 C. An illustrative Base mix at a uniform 30% contingency comprises $900,000 of realized drawback recoveries generating $270,000 fees, $400,000 of realized tariff refunds generating $120,000 fees, and $416,666.67 of actual settlement distributions generating $125,000 fees after cent rounding. Together the fees equal exactly $515,000. The $1,716,666.67 underlying recoveries are client money, not operator sales. The contractual 25%–35% range changes required recovery volume; it does not authorize changing the canonical cases. Where the operator is an agent under ASC 606, assess net presentation using the actual service obligations; do not add gross client proceeds or invent a retained-share multiplier. Treat the scorecard fee basis as fixed and avoid deducting partner compensation twice. Reconcile illustrative automation expenses inside the annual cost envelope rather than adding them again.

Make each distribution experiment purchase measurable evidence, not vanity traffic. At 500 monthly visits and a 2% inquiry rate, a reviewed content cluster yields ten inquiries; if 30% qualify and one-third of those sign, it yields one engagement before recovery uncertainty. Spending $300 on editorial maintenance therefore implies $300 per signed engagement under those assumptions. For the referral example, $200 of monthly partner-support labor divided by two signed engagements equals $100 acquisition labor per engagement, excluding case fulfillment. These channels overlap, so deduplicate contacts and assign one primary source before adding results. Run 100 automated batches monthly at $16.50 including routine QA and the monthly processing budget is $1,650; at twelve months it is $19,800, already contained within the relevant annual cost scenario. Substantive broker preparation, counsel exceptions, surety charges, and operator compensation remain separate cost lines. Keep a thirteen-week cash forecast for expenses and a longer recovery-cohort forecast for delayed receipts. The $8,000–$35,000 startup range and $1,500–$9,500 monthly operating range describe launch planning, not the complete scaled annual cost base. Expand only when measured reviewer capacity, evidence quality, and collected cohort economics support another intake stream. A signed engagement within one to three months is not equivalent to cash collected in that period.

chapters.pull_quote: Automate the evidence trail, not the judgment that makes a recovery collectible.
action_checklist: Create separate drawback, tariff-refund, and settlement ledgers with source-linked eligibility, authority, deadline, bond, and cash fields.
Implement signed webhook intake, versioned document hashes, transactional idempotency keys, and a visible dead-letter queue before enabling unattended runs.
Deploy the SEC trigger play with five-request-per-second aggregate limiting, source-linked human-reviewed outreach, and permitted bulk-archive lookbacks.
Pilot manifest-to-entry matching, export trace reconstruction, eight-digit HTS proposals, and settlement purchase packaging on authorized historical cases.
Measure repetitive minutes before and after automation, include exception rework, and retain human decisions for eligibility, deadlines, submissions, and payment changes.
Reconcile the three canonical profit cases, attribute distribution cohorts without duplicates, and expand only against collected fees and demonstrated reviewer capacity.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #44, Rank #03 of 49, earns a 95/100 Money-to-Manpower Score by turning specialized recovery work into a controlled small-team book. Its 12 mapped plays must share intake, evidence, accounting, and quality controls without merging drawback, tariff refunds, and settled antitrust recoveries. Start with one full-time owner and three contractors; add one employee and one contractor only when measured workloads support them. Canonical annual owner profits are $35,200 Conservative, $231,750 Base, and $533,600 Scaled. This chapter assigns seats, compensation units, weekly indicators, concentration limits, and transfer documentation. Premium exit pricing depends on collectible fee history, replaceable owner labor, licensed filing continuity, and clean rights to operating assets, not the face value of pending claims.

sections.heading: 1. Assign every recovery play to a named seat and an independent release
paragraphs: Build the four-person pod around one full-time owner who owns engagements, capacity, collections, and the weekly exception meeting. Contractor one is a licensed customs broker responsible for customs eligibility, authorized submissions, and regulatory communications. Contractor two is an evidence engineer who normalizes ACE entry exports, CBP Form 7501 records, export bills of lading, and accounts payable ledgers. Contractor three is a recovery analyst who assembles settlement packets, checks supporting schedules, and maintains deadline calendars. These are three contractor seats, not three unlimited service departments. Retain trade counsel for exceptional disputes outside the routine production pod; record that engagement as an incremental cost and disclose any additional staffing it creates. Only the broker or appropriately authorized counsel performs formal customs filings. Unlicensed personnel can prepare factual records but cannot independently perform reserved customs business under 19 CFR Part 111. The owner checks commercial release conditions without overruling professional eligibility decisions. Establish separate permissions for source uploads, working calculations, signed authorities, and submission receipts. ImportGenius and Panjiva identify prospects and shipment patterns; neither replaces importer-controlled entry records. Every case receives one accountable case owner, one qualified reviewer, and one escalation route before evidence production begins. This prevents attractive prospects from becoming owner-only obligations.

Make the 12-play mapping explicit in the operating register rather than treating twelve plays as twelve independent businesses. This chapter uses four operational subplays per lane. Drawback covers D1 direct-identification unused merchandise, D2 substitution unused merchandise, D3 direct-identification manufacturing, and D4 substitution manufacturing. Each requires its own statutory and regulatory analysis; an eight-digit HTS match alone does not establish substitution eligibility. Tariff recovery covers T1 eligible pre-liquidation classification corrections, T2 eligible pre-liquidation origin or preference corrections, T3 timely classification protests, and T4 timely origin, preference, or rate protests. Settlement recovery covers A1 interchange merchant evidence, A2 direct-purchaser purchase evidence, A3 indirect-purchaser evidence where the settlement permits it, and A4 affiliate or successor claim reconciliation. These are workflow mappings, not representations that every transaction qualifies or that every settlement remains open. The broker releases D and T cases; the recovery analyst assembles A cases under the specific court-approved plan and administrator instructions. The evidence engineer supports all twelve through reusable connectors, but each lane keeps distinct eligibility fields and acceptance checklists. The owner approves workload and engagement economics only after those requirements are understood. Do not sell an A4 reconciliation service as permission to submit duplicate claims for the same purchases.

Move to two full-time employees and four contractors by adding an employee delivery lead and a contractor quality specialist. The delivery lead absorbs scheduling, evidence acceptance, and routine client follow-up; the fourth contractor performs sampled reperformance and absence coverage. Qualified customs judgments still require a qualified customs professional. Scale on measured hours, not signed contingency face value. For eight consecutive weeks, track required production hours, available contracted hours, rework, deadline exposure, and cash available for committed labor. An illustrative hiring trigger is sustained utilization above 80% with a funded twelve-week staffing reserve and no overdue statutory tasks. Confirm that the added seats fit the canonical Scaled cost envelope rather than assuming higher revenue absorbs every new expense. Pay the evidence engineer per accepted source batch, the recovery analyst per accepted packet, and the broker through an agreed availability retainer plus case-specific fees. Define acceptance before work starts, including source coverage, reconciliation tolerances, and required reviewer credentials. Avoid paying solely for asserted refunds, which rewards inflated eligibility estimates. Apply employment classification rules to actual working arrangements, including 26 U.S.C. section 3121(d); a contractor label does not settle status. Maintain backup access and documentation without turning independent specialists into unbudgeted full-time employees.

sections.heading: 2. Separate statutory eligibility, bond exposure, and cash clocks by lane
paragraphs: Drawback begins with eligible duties, taxes, and fees actually paid on qualifying imports, not merchandise value or a prospecting database estimate. Under 19 U.S.C. section 1313, many qualifying claims recover 99% of eligible amounts, subject to the applicable subsection and limitations. The broker must verify import and export timing, claimant rights, merchandise treatment, substitution conditions, and prohibited charges. Section 1313(r) generally requires a complete claim within five years after importation; unused-merchandise pathways also impose their own export or destruction timing conditions. Exclude antidumping and countervailing duties under 19 CFR section 190.3, and check the controlling authority for additional tariffs rather than assuming all special duties qualify. Documentation cost includes entry reconstruction, export tracing, inventory reconciliation, manufacturing support where applicable, broker work, and record retention under Part 190. Ordinary processing and accelerated payment are different cash paths. Accelerated payment under section 190.92 requires approval and adequate bond arrangements; a surety quote is not available capacity. Model six to twenty-four months from accepted engagement to receipt as an illustrative planning range, then replace it with actual broker and cohort evidence. Retain repayment exposure in the case register after accelerated cash arrives; payment alone does not remove later examination or liquidation risk.

Tariff refunds require a separate clock and authority map. A Post-Summary Correction is a pre-liquidation ACE correction mechanism, not a protest under 19 U.S.C. section 1514. For eligible entries, the standard PSC operating window is generally within 300 days after entry and at least fifteen days before scheduled liquidation, subject to current CBP rules and entry eligibility. A protest ordinarily must be filed within 180 days after the relevant liquidation or other protestable decision. Record the actual triggering event and qualified review; never substitute an estimated calendar date. The collectible base is the supported overpayment attributable to a defensible correction or protest, excluding unrelated duties and merchandise principal. Documentation cost includes classification analysis, product specifications, origin support, entry reconstruction, and broker or counsel preparation. A refund request generally does not require a separate drawback accelerated-payment bond; existing import bonds and case-specific obligations still need review. Use three to eighteen months after submission as an illustrative ordinary refund planning range, with disputes potentially extending materially longer. Do not describe a denied protest as routine receivables collection. Judicial escalation creates separate standing, payment, timing, and litigation requirements. Price that work separately and prevent routine contractor budgets from silently absorbing contested proceedings.

Settled B2B antitrust recovery follows the court-approved settlement definition, allocation plan, claim form, and deadlines, not customs eligibility. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(e) governs approval of class settlements; the particular order determines qualifying purchasers, products, periods, exclusions, and filing procedures. The collectible base is the claimant's actual allowed distribution, not total purchases, alleged damages, or the settlement fund. Documentation cost includes purchase-ledger extraction, merchant identifiers, affiliate reconciliation, duplicate checks, and administrator responses. No CBP surety bond applies to this lane, although engagement terms or a particular order can impose other requirements. Use six to thirty-six months or longer as an illustrative distribution horizon where allocation, objections, or appeals remain unresolved. Provide required third-party filer disclosures, accurately identify the claimant and authorized representative, and explain that the claimant may file directly at zero cost. Across all lanes, quote the agreed 25%–35% contingency against defined realized recovery. At 30%, a $100,000 eligible distribution produces a $30,000 operator fee and $70,000 for the client before any separately agreed charges. Keep principal outside operator revenue. Prefer direct client receipt and separately invoiced fees; where funds pass through another authorized party, reconcile custody, remittance, and fee deductions explicitly.

sections.heading: 3. Enforce weekly scorecards and reconcile earnings to realized fee cohorts
paragraphs: Run one forty-five-minute weekly meeting from a frozen scorecard exported before discussion. Start with statutory deadlines and evidence defects, then capacity, collections, and concentration. Use stable denominators: first-pass acceptance equals accepted packets without material rework divided by reviewed packets; source coverage equals supported claim lines divided by proposed claim lines. Set an initial 95% first-pass target, require complete source support for released amounts, and require zero unassigned deadlines. These are internal operating targets, not published industry benchmarks. Report both counts and dollars so one large defective claim cannot disappear inside a high packet acceptance percentage. Contractor service terms should require acknowledgment within one business day, triage of a complete intake within two, and ordinary defect correction within three. Shorter statutory windows take priority through an explicit escalation. Pause the service clock only for documented missing inputs, not because a contractor is busy. Sample at least ten percent of routine packets and independently inspect every high-value, novel, or exception case before release. Internal sampling does not replace the broker's professional review. Log root causes against the responsible transformation, checklist, or source system; a corrected spreadsheet without a corrected process simply moves the same defect into next week's batch.

Maintain three linked ledgers: claimant recovery principal, operator fee accounting, and contingent pipeline. The principal ledger follows money owed to clients and never feeds operator sales. The fee ledger records the contractual fee base, rate, performance status, invoice, receipt, and any reversal exposure. The pipeline ledger holds estimates that have not earned recognition. Under ASC 606, evaluate performance obligations and constrain variable consideration until a significant reversal is sufficiently unlikely; signed engagements and submitted claims do not automatically create earned revenue. Apply a documented policy with the accountant, and distinguish recognized revenue, receivables, and bank collections. For this volume, the canonical revenue basis is earned contingency fees on realized recoveries, not gross recovery billings. If another party retains part of the fee, assess principal-versus-agent presentation rather than inventing a retained-share percentage. Accrue contractor costs when services are received even if the claim remains unpaid. Group cases by lane, engagement quarter, submission quarter, and receipt quarter. Reconcile opening receivables plus earned fees less receipts and credits to closing receivables. Report median and seventy-fifth-percentile cash conversion alongside unresolved cohorts; excluding unfinished cases makes slow recovery look artificially efficient. Keep accelerated drawback repayment exposure visible rather than treating every receipt as permanently settled.

Reconcile the operating model to the canonical scorecard without changing its economics. Conservative fee revenue of $110,000 less $74,800 of implied total costs produces $35,200 owner profit at 32%. Base revenue of $515,000 less $283,250 produces $231,750 at 45.0%. Scaled revenue of $920,000 less $386,400 produces $533,600 at 58%. These implied annual costs include the complete modeled cost envelope; the stated $1,500–$9,500 monthly operating range is not a substitute for contractor delivery costs and every other modeled expense. At an illustrative uniform 30% fee, the three revenue levels correspond to approximately $366,666.67, $1,716,666.67, and $3,066,666.67 of realized client recoveries, respectively. Those are supporting unit checks, not new scenarios. Cap each customer group and each commercial counterparty at 25% of trailing-twelve-month earned fees and separately of the probability-weighted twelve-month fee pipeline. Combine related entities and referral-controlled accounts. Treat each settlement pool or administrator dependency as a separate risk concentration, even where clients differ. CBP is an unavoidable sovereign dependency for both customs lanes; disclose that structural concentration rather than claiming importer diversification eliminates it. A breached commercial cap stops incremental exposure to that group while existing obligations continue to be serviced.
